scope: Scoped port pass: exam structure, required practical numbers, tier wrappers, Haber scope, board naming. Not a full fact-check.

findings.claim: The Higher flag wraps the tangent paragraph AND the key fact that gives the gradient equation, the units of rate and the mean rate of reaction.
findings.truth: The mean rate calculation is core, and so is drawing a tangent and using its slope. Only calculating the gradient of a tangent at a specific time is HT only, so the key fact must be visible to Foundation students.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.1.1: 'calculate the mean rate of a reaction...' and 'draw tangents to the curves on these graphs and use the slope of the tangent as a measure of the rate of reaction' are core bullets; '(HT only) calculate the gradient of a tangent... at a specific time' is the only HT clause.

findings.claim: The lesson diagram sits inside the Higher flag, with the condensation polymerisation text.
findings.truth: The diagram covers addition, condensation and natural polymers. Addition polymerisation and the natural polymers are core, so the picture must be visible to Foundation students.
findings.evidence: spec 4.7.3.1 (addition polymerisation) and 4.7.3.4 (DNA and other naturally occurring polymers) carry no HT flag.

findings.claim: The section 'Comparing the Two Types of Polymerisation' sits outside the Higher flag and teaches condensation monomers, the water by-product and named condensation polymers.
findings.truth: Condensation polymerisation is HT only, so this section belongs inside the Higher flag with the rest of that content.

findings.claim: The Haber section tells every student to use Le Chatelier's principle to pick the conditions, but the Le Chatelier section above it is inside a Higher flag.
findings.truth: The Haber process is core for this course, but the trade-off explanation is HT only, so a Foundation student meets the principle here after it was hidden. Option A: wrap that one paragraph in the Higher flag. Option B: leave it, and accept that Foundation students read the reasoning without the principle. Adding a new wrapper to this lesson was outside the instructions for this pass, so it is left for a ruling.
findings.evidence: spec 4.10.4.1 lists the conditions as core and marks '(HT only) ... explain the trade-off between rate of production and position of equilibrium'; spec 4.6.2.4 marks Le Chatelier HT only.

findings.claim: The main text explains the temperature and pressure compromise in full, while a collapsible that repeats the same explanation sits inside a Higher flag.
findings.truth: The conditions are core and the trade-off reasoning is HT only, so the flag is in the right place, but the core body already gives the HT reasoning away. Option A: wrap the two paragraphs that argue the compromise. Option B: drop the flag from the collapsible. Both change more than this pass allows.
findings.evidence: spec 4.10.4.1: conditions core; '(HT only) ... explain the trade-off between rate of production and position of equilibrium'.

findings.claim: Practice questions 3, 4 and 5 and the exam tip all test condensation polymerisation and amino acids.
findings.truth: That content is HT only, but questions and exam tips cannot carry a tier wrapper, so the gate can only be applied to the lesson body.

No lesson gives a practical a number, so no combined-course numbering survived the move. Lesson 1 describes the concentration and rate practical (chemistry number 5) and lesson 4 the paper chromatography practical (chemistry number 6); both methods match the spec. Water purification (number 8) and the ion tests (number 7) appear as content in lessons 7 and 10 but are not labelled as required practicals.

findings.claim: Port check on exam structure, scope sentences and board naming.
findings.truth: No lesson states a paper count, a duration or a mark total, none names an exam board, and none tells students a topic is off their course. Lesson 2 teaches the Haber process as in scope with no disclaimer, which is correct for this course.
findings.evidence: full-text scan of all eleven lessons for 'Combined', 'Trilogy', '70 marks', '1 hour 15', paper counts, board names and out-of-scope phrasing; spec 2.2 and 4.10.4.

summary: The port is already clean on exam structure, required practical numbers, board naming and scope disclaimers. Three tier-wrapper edits follow: lesson 1's Higher flag hid the core mean rate key fact, and lesson 9 hid its diagram while leaving the condensation comparison exposed. The Higher flags in lessons 2, 7, 8 and 11 are confirmed against the chemistry spec (Le Chatelier, alternative metal extraction, strong and weak acids, Haber trade-off).
